headline: Malaysia lets bulk palm oil blends out only on three conditions. A Port Klang complaint tests them
context: Malaysia's 2005 palm oil quality rules bar bulk exports of a blend unless the buyer asked in writing, the contract says so and every shipping paper states the mix. A port agent's complaint about one cargo is with MPOB.

cards.big: Malaysian rules bar exporting a bulk palm oil blend unless the buyer asked for it in writing, the contract says so, and every shipping paper states the mix.
cards.sub: A port agent that signed one cargo's bills of lading, and now seeks an indemnity, alleges they declared the mixed cargo as crude palm olein.
trace: MPOB (Quality) Regulations 2005 reg. 12(1), (3)(a)-(c): 'No person shall sell, export or consign blended oil palm product in bulk or packages exceeding twenty-five kilogrammes' unless requested in writing by the purchaser, specified in the contract of sale, and 'all document of sales, delivery order, shipping documents, bill of lading and customs declaration shall indicate the percentage, ratio, weight or volume of ingredients and compositions of the blend' (Stage 3 VERIFIED as necessary-condition summary; re-read 18 Nov 2026, S1)

Malay Mail 5 Nov 2026 (letter of demand: signed the bills of lading for the master; indemnity sought) [S15]; The Sun/Utusan 17 Nov 2026 (bill of lading changed so 'the entire cargo' was 'declared as crude palm olein') [S16a, S17a]; allegation, unverified (Stage 3 UNVERIFIED, attribution kept)

cards.big: The agent alleges Indonesian palm olein was mixed aboard the tanker MT Eunice at Port Klang on 30 Sep with about 5,000 tonnes of Malaysian crude palm olein.
cards.sub: Its letter says the mix 'remained subject to documentary verification'. We found no ruling on whether the rule covers mixing aboard after loading.
trace: Complainant's account as reported: Malay Mail 5 Nov 2026 (4,999.715 t; letter's 'remained subject to documentary verification'); Utusan and Oriental Daily 17 Nov 2026 (S15, S17a, S17b); Stage 3 UNVERIFIED as fact, attribution accurate
Quality reg. 16 deemed export on loading (Stage 3 VERIFIED); open question on reg. 12 reach: no judgment or official interpretation located (Stage 3; brief WEAKENS 3)

cards.big: For an ordinary Malaysian certificate of origin, one of MITI's three tests is at least 25% local content by value, checked by an authorised chamber.
cards.sub: For cargo only passing through, MITI's transshipment certificate may carry one origin; mixing origins on it is 'totally prohibited'.
trace: MITI NPCO page (updated 22 May 2026): chambers and associations authorised by MITI issue; three alternative criteria incl. 'Contains at least 25% local materials'; chambers 'Check and verify' (Stage 3 VERIFIED; S5a)
MITI Cost Analysis Form: 'At Least QVC 25% Originating Materials', Qualifying Value Content calculation (Stage 3 CORRECTED 'by value'; INTRODUCED, form opened 18 Nov 2026; S5c)

MITI B2B/Transshipment NPCO Guideline, 31 Oct 2017, para 4.2: 'Each B2B NPCO shall only bear one (1) country of origin. Mixture or combination of more than one (1) country of origin in one B2B NPCO is totally prohibited' (Stage 3 VERIFIED; S5b)

cards.big: MPOB must table a yearly activities report in Parliament, but no rule makes it announce single cases, and its Act limits disclosure to the Act's purposes.
cards.sub: Its 2005 compounding list covers untrue declarations, not quality-rule offences like blending. We found no MPOB statement of its own on this case.
trace: Act 582 s. 37 applies Act 240; Act 240 s. 7 (report of activities to the Minister each financial year) and s. 8 (laid on the table of each House) (Stage 3 omitted fact; INTRODUCED, both texts opened 18 Nov 2026; S3a, S3d)
Act 582 s. 66(1) disclosure 'Except for the purposes of this Act'; no section requiring publication of case outcomes (Stage 3 VERIFIED; S3a)
MPOB (Compounding of Offences) Regulations 2005 Schedule: Act s. 67 and Licensing offences; no Quality Regulations offence (Stage 3 VERIFIED, reproduced schedule; S2c)
No standalone MPOB statement found to 18 Nov 2026; MPOB Palm News reposted The Sun's report on 18 Nov (clipping, not an MPOB statement) (Stage 3; S7c)

cards.big: MPOB both champions Malaysian palm oil and polices it. The law asks it to account to Parliament once a year, not to explain any single case.
trace: Act 582 s. 3(2)(a) objective 'to promote and develop the oil palm industry'; s. 4(d) function to regulate export and import (Stage 3 VERIFIED; coexistence does not by itself prove compromised enforcement, not claimed)

cards.big: Four weeks' quiet on a cross-border cargo can pass as routine. When the 'Malaysian' label carries the industry's imprimatur, a word on the file's status costs less than silence.
trace: Complaint lodged 19 Oct 2026; MPOB reply reported dated 22 Oct; no MPOB statement of its own found to 18 Nov (S16a, S17a). View is editorial opinion; it makes no legal claim about what s. 66 permits.

introduced_claims.claim: MPOB must table a yearly activities report in Parliament
introduced_claims.primary_source: Act 582 s. 37 ('The Statutory Bodies (Accounts and Annual Reports) Act 1980 shall apply to the Board'), FAOLEX text; Act 240 s. 7 ('Every statutory body shall, in respect of each financial year ... submit ... to the Minister together with a report of its activities') and s. 8 ('The Minister shall ... cause the same to be laid on the table of each House of Parliament'), AGC reprint, both opened 18 Nov 2026.

introduced_claims.primary_source: MITI Cost Analysis Form for NPCO, opened 18 Nov 2026: 'At Least QVC 25% Originating Materials'; 'Qualifying Value Content (QVC) Calculation'; 'Calculation of local contents (at least 25 %)'.

synthesis_notes: Over-integration calls. (1) Stage 2 wanted the complainant's own legal exposure stated more strongly (UNDERCLAIM); Stage 3 rated every case fact UNVERIFIED. The evidence supports stating the complainant's role and stake (signed the bills of lading; seeks an indemnity) and its own caveat; it does not support asserting what liability a signatory faces, which no opened source states. Kept to the sourced facts. (2) Stage 2 asked to add Customs, MSPO, smallholders and East Malaysia. Customs and East Malaysia: the rules described are national and the cards no longer generalise from Port Klang; Customs holds the customs declaration that reg. 12(3)(c) names (in trace). MSPO and smallholders: no primary source ties this complaint to MSPO or to smallholder prices; the only such link is an anonymous industry quote and the complainant's own statement, which fail the bar. Recorded, not added. (3) Stage 3 supplied MPOB Annual Report 2023 enforcement totals (3,642 compound actions; 35 completed prosecution cases) as an omitted fact; the parliament repository refused the connection on three attempts and no other copy was found, so the figures stay off the cards. They would strengthen the reframe's 'once a year' point if verified before Phase 8. Compression decisions. Hook keeps all three reg. 12 conditions; 'sell' and 'consign' are folded into 'exporting' (the case concerns an export). Fact 2 drops the 100%-local and tariff-shift tests and names them only as 'one of three tests'. The imports series (2025 three times 2024 but below 2020-2023) stays off the cards. The gazette identifiers (P.U.(A) 518/2005 vs 79/2006; 519/2005 vs 80/2006) are disclosed in the brief SOURCES and never shown on cards. Stage 5: not triggered.
